raw_case_text:
A 52-year-old male patient referred to the infectious clinic of Shohadaye Ashayer Hospital in the Lorestan province of Iran. He complained about several ulcerative lesions on the back of his fingers (Figure 1). Both hands were involved. However, the ulcers were limited to the back of his fingers, not being observed on the palmar surface of his hands. The wrist, the forearm, and the rest of his upper limbs were not involved, either. The patient mentioned that his ulcers were not itchy, but they were painful. He did not complain about pain in his joints, but he had experienced fever and sweating, at times intense, particularly at nights. He stated that he had lost 5 kg of weight during the course of his disease. Neither the patient himself nor his family members had been affected by chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and so on. He had not taken any medications for a long period of time and was neither a smoker nor an addict. He said that he was a farmer.
On physical examination, he was conscious and his vital signs were stable. There was no organomegaly. Motor and sensory examination of the upper and lower limbs was normal. His pulse was normal. The only findings detected during physical examination were a high temperature and ulcerative lesions on his fingers.
The results of the laboratory tests were as follows: The hematology test showed that the white blood cell count was 9500/microL (neutrophils 65%, lymphocytes 27%, monocytes 5%, and eosinophils 3%), the red blood cell count was 5.51 x 106/microL, the platelet count was 266 x 103/microL, Hb was 17 g/dL, hematocrit was 49%, MCV was 88 fL, ESR 1st hour was 5, and so on. The biochemistry test showed that urea was 26 mg/dl, creatinine was 0.9 mg/dl, calcium was 9.9 mg/dl, TSH was 1.0 ulU/ml, T3 was 0.8 ng/ml, and T4 was 8.9 microg/dl. In the immunoassay tests, HIV and the hepatitis virus panel showed that HBsAg was negative and HIV Ag. Ab" I + II and HCV Ab were both nonreactive. The serology test showed that CRP was negative but the Wright agglutination test and 2ME (the Wright agglutination test is the first step in diagnosis of brucellosis, and the 2ME test is used as a complementary test) were both positive, being 1/60 and 1/80, respectively. Hereby, it was confirmed that ulcerative lesions on the fingers of the patient were due to infection with brucellosis. Therefore, standard antibiotic treatment for the patient was prescribed, and his lesions started to heal in a short period of time.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 52-year-old male farmer presented with painful, non-pruritic ulcerative lesions on the dorsal aspects of his fingers, nocturnal sweating, fever, and 5 kg weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with several painful, non-pruritic ulcerative lesions strictly localized to the dorsal aspects of the fingers of both hands, sparing the palmar surfaces, wrists, and forearms. He experienced fever and intense sweating, particularly nocturnal, and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg during the disease course. He denied joint pain.
subjective.past_medical_history: No chronic medical conditions (hypertension, diabetes denied); no family history of chronic illnesses. Denied smoking, illicit drug use, or long-term medication use. Occupation/Epidemiological exposure: farmer in Lorestan Province, Iran.
subjective.review_of_systems: Painful skin ulcers on fingers, night sweats, fever, 5 kg weight loss. Denied joint pain or pruritus. Home medications: none. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Conscious, stable vital signs with elevated body temperature (fever); pulse normal. Cutaneous exam: multiple painful ulcerative lesions on the dorsum of fingers bilaterally without palmar, wrist, or forearm extension. Abdomen: no organomegaly (hepatosplenomegaly absent). Neurological exam: motor and sensory examinations of upper and lower limbs normal.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 9,500/microL (65% neutrophils, 27% lymphocytes, 5% monocytes, 3% eosinophils), RBC 5.51 x 106/microL, platelets 266 x 103/microL, hemoglobin 17 g/dL, hematocrit 49%, MCV 88 fL, ESR 1st hour 5 mm/hr. Biochemistry: urea 26 mg/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, calcium 9.9 mg/dL. Thyroid panel: TSH 1.0 ulU/mL, T3 0.8 ng/mL, T4 8.9 microg/dL. Inflammatory and viral serologies: CRP negative; HBsAg negative, HCV Ab nonreactive, HIV Ag/Ab combo nonreactive.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Cutaneous brucellosis manifesting as dorsal digital ulcerative lesions. Confirmed by positive Wright agglutination test (titer 1/60) and 2-mercaptoethanol (2ME) agglutination test (titer 1/80). Viral hepatitides and HIV excluded.
Plan & Outcome: Prescribed standard anti-Brucella antibiotic therapy, with rapid onset of ulcer healing and clinical improvement over a short period.
